context_documents.title: 2022-4499 · Collapsible acquisition and lowered transport preserve packaging
context_documents.body:
# 2022-4499: Collapsible acquisition and lowered transport preserve packaging

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A wide compliant four-bar feeds a lowered second stage and a fixed-heading adjustable-hood launcher. The compact climb replaces an earlier size-constrained concept. A central transport feature remains from a dual-intake idea that was not built.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly wants the collector to collapse in wall contact, especially behind the hub where visibility is poor; climb packaging motivated the alternate arrangement.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A visible legacy feature is not proof of a fielded subsystem. Collector compliance must work with the pneumatic state and hard stops, while a lower transport path can alter compression and dead zones.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test blind-side contact, full-path flow and climb/shooter clearance; retain the unbuilt dual-intake status.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/U0vM488i2Lg](https://youtu.be/U0vM488i2Lg)

source_reviews.title: The Highlanders 2022 Technical Binder
source_reviews.locator: pp. 3–13, especially feeder iterations p. 7 and climb p. 9
source_reviews.review_basis: Re-read indexed binder text, specifications and figure descriptions through web retrieval.
facts: MK4 L2 swerve, two-roller intake, two-station beam-break sensing, a printed double-sided feeder ramp, powered shooter hood and chain-driven climber are documented.
The binder separates an unstable first feeder with a flexing ramp from the revised flat deck and speed bump. The arm and elevator have separate motors and reductions.
The team describes camera-aided hub positioning, swerve path interpolation and combining several position estimates.
limitations: The binder reports subsystem specs and objectives. Its one-second loaded extension claim is for the elevator stroke. Full climb time and event-by-event hardware were not verified.
Binder identifies an OAK-D in the shooting system. Camera substitutions or other configurations require separate evidence.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Maverick collects from one side with a pair of full-width rollers, funnels cargo into a low two-ball feeder and shoots with a powered adjustable hood. Heading comes from the chassis, which can translate independently of yaw. Endgame is a separate elevator-and-arm system tied structurally into both the feeder superstructure and chassis. The low cargo deck and centered climb address different mass and load cases.
source_review.piece_flow: Floor cargo first meets the compliant pickup rollers, rides up and over the bumper, and is centered by rear mecanum elements and feeder flaps. Front feeder wheels move it across the flat deck toward the central bump, which brings the ball up into the indexing wheels. Inlet and outlet beam breaks observe flow and staging. The index wheels hold or advance cargo into the flywheels. The moving hood defines exit geometry and the mechanically driven rear roller acts on spin. The binder establishes capacity of two and an indexed release, with exact two-ball positions and spacing logic unresolved.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The nonparallel four-bar changes the roller pose between pickup and retraction. Feeder compression is concentrated at the bump, letting most of the transport remain low. The elevator carriage translates while the separate arm rotates, and chassis yaw steers shot azimuth. Check the arm sweep against the hood envelope and trace whether structural distortion during a hang could shift the indexing gap.

subsystems.name: Chassis and aiming
subsystems.construction: Square tube chassis, standardized mounting holes, inner electronics routing, MK4 L2 modules with four-inch nitrile-tread wheels.
subsystems.operation: Swerve accepts planar and angular velocities. Hub vision contributes position information alongside gyro heading and odometry.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team valued agile movement around the hub, straightforward integration and early time for other subsystems.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A fixed-azimuth launcher makes chassis yaw accuracy a shot variable. Swerve can set yaw while translating, although intake approach still constrains where the chassis points.
subsystems.interfaces: Drive mounting, common feeder and climb references, hub camera and gyro.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect tread and verify yaw references after contact. Camera bias or wheel slip can shift both path following and the shot setup.
subsystems.unknowns: Full aiming gate and camera calibration parameters.

subsystems.name: Intake
subsystems.construction: Two belt-driven aluminum rollers on a pneumatic nonparallel four-bar with quarter-inch polycarbonate plates. One Falcon drives the rollers.
subsystems.operation: Compliant wheels collect and rear mecanum ends steer cargo inward before the handoff.
subsystems.team_rationale: Survive impacts, collect at speed and retract around defenders.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Soft wheel contact and yielding links address different disturbances. The rear lateral component only helps if the second roller still has traction as the ball clears the bumper.
subsystems.interfaces: Bumper clearance, feeder inlet and paired cylinder linkage.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect both sides for skew and the shared belt for damage after corner impacts.
subsystems.unknowns: Deployed gaps and any cylinder synchronization procedure.

subsystems.name: Feeder
subsystems.construction: Flat deck, printed double-sided bump, flaps, two-inch entrance wheels, three-inch compliant index wheels and two beam breaks.
subsystems.operation: The bump lifts cargo into the indexing nip just upstream of the launcher.
subsystems.team_rationale: Preserve a low two-ball package and stable grip while allowing a possible second collector.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A localized rigid rise makes indexing compression less sensitive to long-deck flex. Too much squeeze can turn two-ball acquisition into a stall.
subsystems.interfaces: Intake exit, two sensor stations, launcher throat and feeder frame supporting the climber.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check ramp fasteners, sensor alignment and wheel wear before changing control timing.
subsystems.unknowns: Compression tolerance for worn cargo and exact occupancy state machine.

subsystems.name: Shooter
subsystems.construction: Two six-inch nitrile-tread flywheels, two Falcon motors, a geared hood and a two-inch backspin roller driven from the flywheel.
subsystems.operation: Changes RPM and elevation for range, with the chassis positioning for the shot.
subsystems.team_rationale: Repeatable fast shots from multiple ranges.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Coupling rear contact speed to the main wheel reduces independent tuning variables. Wear can still change the effective ratio at the ball.
subsystems.interfaces: Indexer entry, camera-derived pose and hood position.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check tread, belt and hood play when a range-map correction fails to repeat.
subsystems.unknowns: Measured exit spin, per-range settings and accuracy under contact.

subsystems.name: Climber
subsystems.construction: Two-stage elevator on tube rails, #25H chain drive, two Falcons, one-way carriage hooks and separately geared NEO 550 rotating arm.
subsystems.operation: Carriage and arm reach and transfer rung contact. Ratcheting hooks retain the robot after the match.
subsystems.team_rationale: Compact packaging and centering near the center of mass to reduce lateral swing.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Rail alignment and chain tension matter under off-axis loading. The feeder structure is part of the climb load path.
subsystems.interfaces: Rung to hooks, rails and feeder/chassis tubes.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check bearing preload, chain slack, hook closure and hard-stop damage after an asymmetric catch.
subsystems.unknowns: Full rung transfer state sequence, swing feedback implementation and loaded approach statistics.

revisions: First feeder used a belt and flexible sheet ramp. Its successor used a flat plane and a raised indexing bump. Dual-side provision remained a packaging option in the binder.
transferable_principles: Measure compression at a repeatable index point, and include feeder supports in any loaded climb fixture that represents this frame.
disconfirming_conditions: A central bump loses its advantage if cargo stacks at the convergence or if climb loads move the roller reference. A fixed-azimuth shot loses cycle time if chassis yaw is repeatedly blocked.
remaining_gaps: Event camera chronology, complete climb sequence, achieved approach-to-hang timing and indexed-feed performance on worn cargo.

recommended_images.purpose: Published intake, feeder path and shooter diagrams for the over-bumper handoff and indexed release.
